newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador banker pleased with new S&P rating.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador banker pleased with new S&P rating.

text.p: The leader of El Salvador's top banking association on Tuesday praised the risk ratings that Standard & Poor's assigned to this Central American country.

S&P on Tuesday assigned El Salvador a BB long-term risk rating and a B short-term risk rating for dollar investments. S&P also gave a BBB-plus rating to long-term Salvadoran debt and A2 for short-term debt in the local colon currency.

"The news that El Salvador has achieved this international level tells the world that the country enjoys sustainable economic stability, which should translate into an increase in foreign investment," said Archie Baldocchi, president of the Association of Salvadoran Bankers.
Baldocchi said the rating also should help the government win international loans on more favorable terms.

More than 70,000 Salvadorans, many of the civilians, were killed in a 12-year civil war that set back the economy of this small Central American country until a peace was signed in 1992. Since then El Salvador's economy has grown faster than those of neighboring countries also engulfed in a regional conflict during the Cold War era.
